name: Delicate Arch
description: Welcome to PACK OUT! For your first trek, you figured you'd start small. Delicate Arch is 1 or 2 hour desert day hike at Arches National Park. The 52-foot tall, free-standing natural arch is famous as a Utah state icon and for its sunset views. This hike's exposed slickrock offers no shade. Pack enough water and get moving.

name: Fish Lake Loop
description: Fish Lake is Utah's largest natural mountain lake, located at over 8,800 feet in the Fishlake National Forest. Known as the 'gem of Utah,' this 5-mile long and 1-mile wide alpine lake is famous for large lake trout and year-round fishing. It is also home to Pando, a massive clonal colony of a single male Quaking Aspen located in the Fishlake National Forest in south-central Utah. While it looks like a forest of 47,000 individual trees, it is actually one single living organism connected by a vast, shared underground root system. You had to check this place out, so you set out for a long day hike around the lake's perimeter. Pack enough food and water to stay strong through the full loop.

name: Lake Blanche
description: You're finally feeling comfortable enough to plan your first single-night backpacking trip. Lake Blanche is a popular, scenic alpine lake backpacking destination in Utah's Wasatch Mountains, known for its steep, 6.7 to 7-mile round-trip hike, and stunning views of Sundial Peak. You will need more than food and water to make it through the night.

name: Glacier National Park
description: Glacier National Park features over 700 miles of hiking trails, the famous, scenic Going-to-the-Sun Road, and is home to the 'Triple Divide Peak,' where water can flow to the Pacific, Atlantic, or Arctic Oceans. You're planning a 3-night traverse across some of the most rugged terrain North America. Snow lingers well into summer and the weather turns fast. Every pound in your pack will cost you.

name: Olympic National Park
description: Olympic National Park plays host to mountains, ocean, rivers, and rainforests; providing bountiful opportunities for recreation and learning. You will take a week-long traverse through rainforest, river valleys, and alpine ridges. You will cover 50 miles over 7 days in some of the wettest terrain in the lower 48. Everything you have learned will be tested.
